segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name's Dan Pearman and I'd like to talk about the work of Pedal Power, a small charity based mainly in the UK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'll be giving our contact details at the end, if anyone would like to find out more about how to support us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But first, how the charity began.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I got the idea of exporting bicycles to developing countries while I was in Ecuador.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I went there in 1993 just after graduating from university.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: After three years of studying, I wanted adventure.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I loved travelling, so 1 decided to join a voluntary organisation and was sent to Ecuador to carry out land surveys.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The project came to an end after five years and when 1 returned to the UK in 1998, I started planning Pedal Power.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Where I lived in Ecuador was a very rural area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My neighbour had the only bicycle in the village, whereas everyone else walked everywhere.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My neighbour's business was unusually successful, and for years I couldn't understand why.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then I realised having a bike meant he could get where he wanted to go without much trouble.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Other local carpenters could only accept jobs in a three-kilometre radius, so no matter how skilled they were, they could never do as many jobs as my neighbour.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At Pedal Power, we collect second-hand bikes in the UK and send them to some of the poorest regions in the world.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When we distribute bikes overseas we don't give them away for free.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We'd like to, but long term that doesn't really help the local economy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The demand for bikes is enormous, which makes them very expensive locally.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So we sell them for 5% of the normal price.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But in order to continue operating we need to have a constant supply of bikes which we send out every six months.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One of a town that's received bicycles from Pedal Power is Rivas.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was the first place I sent a full container of bicycles to.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most people there now own a bicycle.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The local economy has developed so much. you wouldn't recognise it as the same place.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In fact, there are more bikes than on the streets of Amsterdam, if you've ever been there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But Pedal Power still needs your help.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may have read about some of our recent problems in the British media.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In August 2000, we simply ran out of money.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We had containers of bikes ready to send, but no money to pay the bills.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was a terrible situation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We managed to ensure the bikes went out on time, but the other problems carried on for several months.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Fortunately in October 2001 we won an Enterprise Award which helped us enormously.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We invested fifteen of the seventy-five-thousand-pound prize money to help secure our future.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Winning the award helped raise our profile, and the money enabled us to pay all our shipping costs, which represent our greatest expense.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Pedal Power changes lives - when someone gets a bicycle from us, they see a 14% increase in their income.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We're currently looking to invest in computers so that our office staff can do an even better job.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Because of our work, people in a number of countries now have a better standard of living- so far we've provided 46,000 people with bikes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But we'd like to send more, at least 50,000 by the end of the year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now there are many ways in which you can support the work of Pedal Power, not just by taking a bike to a collection in your area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I should also like to say if you do have a bike to donate, it doesn't matter what condition it's in - if we can't repair it, we'll strip it down for spare parts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Of course, to do that we always need tools, which are expensive /19/20 to buy, so we welcome any that you can give.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Also, you could help by contacting the voluntary staff at our offices, they'll be able to suggest activities you could organise to / 19/20 bring in funds for us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: People do all kinds of things - including, of course, sponsored bike rides.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Also, we're always interested to hear of other places that would benefit from /19/20 receiving a consignment of bikes, and welcome suggestions from people who've been to developing regions on their travels.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We hope that by talking on radio programmes like this, we will be able to raise public awareness, which will lead to government organisations also giving us regular financial support, something that we really need.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you'd like some more information about where to donate an old bicycle or offer help in other ways please contact us on ...
